title: Paying Your Home-Site Lease: When Payments Are Accepted and How They Are Applied
content:
**Home-Site Lease — terms for payments toward the lease ledger**

**On which leases a payment is accepted.** Payments are accepted on a lease that is active, notice to vacate, in default, or closed with a balance still owing; nothing is accepted on an application. The status is read from the lease record of the lease being paid.

**Through which channels.** A payment arriving through a channel outside the lot class's accepted channels is refused, except that a past-due balance paid from the proceeds of an in-place home sale is posted on the closing date as sale closing proceeds.

**Certified-funds-only status — no longer in force.** The former clause by which, while the lease is on certified-funds-only status and the payment date is on or before the last day of that status, only a payment through one of the lot class's certified-funds channels is accepted, is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis.

**Amount before a nonpayment notice.** Before a nonpayment notice is served, a payment of any amount is accepted.

**Amount after a nonpayment notice — no longer in force.** The former clause by which, after a nonpayment notice is served and until it is cured, a payment smaller than the amount demanded is refused, is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis.

**Posting and application.** A payment is posted on the date it is received and applied in the lot class's application order — returned-payment fees, then late fees, then other fees, then the oldest rent and occupant charges first.

**Overpayment.** An overpayment stays on the ledger as a credit balance against later charges and is refunded only with the deposit disposition after the lease closes.

### Questions answered by these terms

*Can an applicant prepay rent before the lease is signed?* No. Nothing is accepted on an application.

*Can a former resident pay a balance after the lease has closed?* Yes, while a balance is still owing on the closed lease.

*If a resident pays more than is owed, is the extra refunded?* Not while the lease is open; it remains a credit balance against later charges and is refunded with the deposit disposition after the lease closes.

*Hypothetical application of a payment of 150.00* against a 35.00 returned-payment fee, a 50.00 late fee and 700.00 of rent: 35.00 clears the returned-payment fee, 50.00 clears the late fee and the remaining 65.00 goes to the oldest rent.

superseded_clauses: After a nonpayment notice is served and until it is cured, a payment smaller than the amount demanded is refused, because partial_payment_accepted_after_nonpayment_notice is false.
While the lease is on certified_funds_only status and the payment date is on or before certified_funds_until, only a payment through one of the certified_funds_channels is accepted.
